title: Samarra’s Abbasid capital takes shape
summary: Samarra on the Tigris became an Abbasid imperial centre with major architectural works. Its ninth-century Great Mosque and spiral minaret remain visible elements of a much larger archaeological city.

Ninth-century architectural phase; source does not identify an exact day.

Capital building can concentrate resources and artistic experimentation. Samarra offers a regional counterpart to contemporary monumental projects in East and Southeast Asia without implying that they shared a direct relationship.
